content.title: Why not just return `any`?
Read the angle brackets

options.text: Every result must contain a number.
Whatever type goes in becomes the type of the `value` property in the result.
Generic functions can accept only objects.

feedback.correct: The generic parameter connects the input type to the output shape.
feedback.incorrect: The generic parameter connects the input type to the output shape.

content.title: When generics are useful
content.text:
Generics are useful when you have a reusable operation whose logic stays the same while the value type changes.

They are not a contest for how many angle brackets you can fit into one function.

A good first question is:

**“What relationship between input and output do I want to preserve?”**

content.question: Which statement best explains a generic type parameter?

options.text: It means the function only works with strings.
It lets a function stay reusable while preserving useful relationships between types.
It automatically makes every value nullable.

feedback.correct: Generics preserve relationships. They are useful when the same operation should work across many types without throwing away type information.
feedback.incorrect: Generics preserve relationships. They are useful when the same operation should work across many types without throwing away type information.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** A generic is a placeholder for a type that lets reusable code keep the relationship between what goes in and what comes out.
**Senior habit:** Before reaching for a generic, identify the relationship you need to preserve. If there is no useful relationship, a generic may just add noise.
